paragraphs: A system that separates individual objects in a 3D room usually learns a fixed list of categories. This paper studies a broader setting: the system should recognize familiar categories, mark unfamiliar objects as unknown, and later learn their categories when labels become available. This makes recognizing uncertainty part of the segmentation task.

The proposed method creates provisional labels automatically during training. These pseudo-labels help the model separate known categories from unknown ones. At inference, it further adjusts the probability of the unknown class using the distribution of objectness scores, which indicate whether a candidate corresponds to an object. This adjustment aims to improve pseudo-label quality.

The researchers also construct evaluation splits reflecting object distributions, exploration of different indoor regions, and randomly selected unknown classes. Their experiments report promising performance and support the effectiveness of the proposed components. The contribution combines a method with evaluation settings for studying how 3D segmentation can accommodate objects whose category labels arrive after initial training.
neurips-2023-3d-indoor-instance-segmenta.tldr: The paper develops 3D indoor object segmentation that identifies unknown objects and can learn their categories when labels become available.

paragraphs: Sampling from a non-convex distribution is important for probabilistic inference and for methods connected to deep learning optimization. A central theoretical question concerns the final step of a sampling algorithm: does its distribution approach the intended target? The paper addresses gaps in such last-iterate guarantees, particularly for methods beyond elementary stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics.

The authors develop a framework using dynamical systems theory. Its main result connects discrete sampling algorithms to their continuous-time counterparts. For a large class of advanced schemes, proving last-iterate convergence in Wasserstein distance can be reduced to studying the corresponding continuous-time process. Wasserstein distance supplies a way to measure how closely two probability distributions agree.

Combined with standard assumptions used in Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling, the framework gives last-iterate convergence results for mirror Langevin, proximal, randomized midpoint, and Runge-Kutta methods. Its significance is a shared route to analyzing several sophisticated algorithms. The guarantees remain conditional on the sampling assumptions and apply to the class of schemes covered by the framework.
neurips-2023-a-dynamical-system-view-of-.tldr: A dynamical systems framework establishes conditional last-iterate convergence guarantees for a broad class of advanced Langevin-based samplers.

paragraphs: Antibody generation involves choosing both a molecular sequence and the three-dimensional structure associated with it. AbDiffuser tackles these choices jointly with a diffusion model. Its design incorporates physical constraints and domain knowledge, aiming to make the iterative denoising process better suited to proteins and to generate both their backbones and side chains.

The method combines a new protein structure representation, an architecture designed for aligned proteins, and strong diffusion priors. It also accommodates changes in sequence length. The authors report an order-of-magnitude reduction in memory complexity, which enables generation at the backbone and side-chain level. These components connect the model's computational design to the structural detail it can produce.

Evaluation includes computational tests and laboratory experiments. Generated antibodies closely follow the sequence and structural properties of a reference collection in the numerical experiments. In the laboratory, all 16 discovered HER2 antibodies were expressed at high levels, and 57.1% of selected designs were tight binders. Those findings demonstrate laboratory function for tested designs while keeping expression and binding success as distinct outcomes.
neurips-2023-abdiffuser-full-atom-genera.tldr: AbDiffuser jointly generates antibody sequences and full-atom structures, with computational validation and laboratory evidence of expression and binding.

paragraphs: Two photographs can show the same object while differing greatly in lighting, pose, or background. This paper asks how to compare images using the properties that define the object's identity. It extends the re-identification problem beyond commonly studied categories such as people and cars toward a wider range of everyday objects.

To evaluate this idea, the researchers introduce CUTE, a dataset containing 18,000 images of 180 objects photographed under varying external conditions. They find that existing LPIPS and CLIP similarity scores do not capture intrinsic object similarity well. Their approach combines features learned through contrastive self-supervised learning with foreground filtering, helping the comparison concentrate on the object.

An extensive comparison of pretrained features and foreground extraction methods produces a strong baseline for this form of similarity measurement. The authors also demonstrate uses as an analog for human subjects and for improving generalizable re-identification. The findings support a practical approximation to identity-focused similarity: selecting suitable features and restricting attention to the foreground can improve comparisons across changes in imaging conditions.
neurips-2023-are-these-the-same-apple-co.tldr: A new dataset and feature-based comparison method assess whether images show the same object despite changes in lighting, pose, and background.

paragraphs: Mechanism design must often balance social welfare with the revenue collected by the designer. This paper develops a method for improving both using side information about agents' types. That information may come from machine learning, experts, or informal judgment. The framework makes no assumption that this information is correct or comes from a particular source.

The proposed meta-mechanism combines side information with an improvement of the classical VCG mechanism. Its analysis introduces constructions based on a weakest competitor: an agent whose presence has the smallest effect on welfare. These constructions characterize welfare, revenue, and incentive properties, allowing performance guarantees to be expressed in terms of errors in the supplied information.

When the information is highly accurate and informative, suitable instances achieve welfare and revenue competitive with total social surplus. The guarantees deteriorate gradually as information quality falls. The authors also obtain guarantees when agent types lie in known constant-dimensional subspaces, even if the surrounding type space is large. That application relies specifically on the designer knowing those subspaces.
neurips-2023-bicriteria-multidimensional.tldr: A mechanism-design framework uses potentially inaccurate side information to obtain joint welfare and revenue guarantees that depend on information quality.

paragraphs: A pretrained reinforcement learning policy can contain a backdoor that changes its behavior when an attack trigger appears. BIRD addresses the problem of detecting and removing such backdoors after training. It works with the policy in a clean environment, without requiring access to the original training process or prior knowledge of the attack specifications.

The method analyzes properties and behaviors associated with backdoor attacks and turns trigger restoration into an optimization problem. It then uses a newly designed metric to identify backdoored policies. A separate fine-tuning procedure aims to remove the backdoor while preserving the agent's performance in the clean environment, connecting detection with a corrective action.

The authors evaluate BIRD against three attacks across ten environments involving either a single agent or multiple agents. They report effectiveness, efficiency, generalizability, and robustness to tested attack variations and adaptations. These results support its use across the evaluated settings. Access to a clean environment remains part of the stated setup, even though knowledge of the attack and the policy's training history is unnecessary.
neurips-2023-bird-generalizable-backdoor.tldr: BIRD detects and removes backdoors from pretrained reinforcement learning policies using a clean environment without needing attack specifications or training access.

paragraphs: Relational knowledge distillation trains a student model to reproduce relationships among a teacher model's features. Although this approach works empirically, its theoretical explanation is less developed. This paper studies why it can help semi-supervised classification, where unlabeled examples accompany a limited supply of labels, by connecting the learning process to clustering.

The authors interpret relational distillation as spectral clustering on a graph induced by the population through the teacher model. They define an error measuring disagreement between predicted and true clusters and prove low clustering error for the population version of the problem. They also derive a sample complexity bound describing the finite-unlabeled-data setting.

A broader framework then connects low clustering error to label-efficient semi-supervised learning. This part explicitly assumes that clustering errors are small. Within the same framework, the authors place consistency regularization based on data augmentation. Both approaches can learn accurate clusters, but the analysis distinguishes distillation's global spectral perspective from consistency regularization's local expansion perspective, clarifying how their routes to useful structure differ.
neurips-2023-cluster-aware-semi-supervis.tldr: The paper explains relational knowledge distillation through spectral clustering and connects low clustering error to label-efficient semi-supervised learning.

paragraphs: Cold Diffusion investigates which parts of a diffusion model are responsible for its ability to generate images. Standard diffusion models degrade an image by adding Gaussian noise, then use a restoration operator to reverse that degradation. The paper asks how much the resulting generative behavior depends on choosing noise as the degradation process.

The authors vary the image transformation and generalize the training and generation update rules to accommodate other degradations. These include deterministic operations such as blurring and masking: transformations that do not themselves require random noise. This produces a family of generative models organized around different ways of degrading and restoring images.

The reported success of these deterministic models suggests that generative behavior is not strongly tied to the particular degradation chosen. That finding challenges explanations of diffusion models that place noise at the center through Langevin dynamics or variational inference. It supports exploring a broader framework for generation through reversing transformations, while the abstract presents inversion of arbitrary processes as a direction opened by the work rather than a demonstrated guarantee for every process.
neurips-2023-cold-diffusion-inverting-ar.tldr: Cold Diffusion shows that diffusion-style generative models can use deterministic degradations such as blur and masking, challenging explanations centered on noise.

paragraphs: Digital human avatars need both convincing appearance and fast rendering, especially when their motion is controllable. The paper identifies achieving these properties together as a continuing challenge. DELIFFAS addresses it by attaching a representation of human appearance to a controllable mesh that deforms with the person, tying appearance generation directly to the changing body geometry.

The representation is a surface light field built around the human using two deformable surfaces. This parameterization enables fast, accurate inference of appearance. Its speed also changes how the model can be trained: the authors can apply perceptual supervision to complete images, whereas slower previous approaches could supervise only individual pixels or small patches.

The contribution therefore links representation efficiency with the scope of the training signal. Full-image supervision can evaluate appearance at the image level while the deforming mesh supplies control over the avatar. The authors report state-of-the-art synthesis results and inference time from this combination. Their stated finding concerns the joint design of the human representation and supervision strategy.
neurips-2023-deliffas-deformable-light-f.tldr: DELIFFAS combines deformable surface light fields with full-image supervision to produce controllable human avatars quickly and photorealistically.

paragraphs: Digital Typhoon provides more than forty years of satellite imagery for studying tropical cyclones with machine learning. The paper presents its official release as a benchmark for data that vary across both space and time. Its long record supports research that must consider storms across many observations and across changing satellite measurement conditions.

The dataset construction workflow produces infrared images centered on each typhoon. It uses best-track information and a Lambert azimuthal equal-area projection to prepare the image crops. The authors also address quality issues, including calibration between satellites, to make the collection homogeneous. These processing choices matter because comparability across the record is central to using a long-term dataset.

The paper organizes potential tasks by inference type and target, including meteorological analysis and questions about societal impacts and climate change. Benchmarks on intensity analysis, forecasting, and reanalysis suggest that recent deep learning models still find the dataset challenging, with performance affected by many choices. Public release lowers the access barrier for researchers, with possible contributions to cyclone science and disaster reduction.
neurips-2023-digital-typhoon-long-term-s.tldr: Digital Typhoon releases a calibrated, typhoon-centered satellite image record spanning over forty years for challenging spatial and temporal machine learning tasks.

paragraphs: In-context image captioning gives a vision-language model example image-caption pairs before asking it to describe another image. This paper examines how the choice and arrangement of those examples affect performance. It responds to a practice of randomly sampling pairs, despite the wider exploration of context configuration strategies for language-only models.

The authors design four strategies for selecting images and four strategies for assigning captions. Separating these decisions allows them to examine how the visual and textual parts of the context work together. Image captioning serves as the case study because producing a caption can be viewed as language modeling conditioned on visual input.

The experiments yield two findings the authors describe as counterintuitive and connect to interaction between modalities, although the abstract does not specify their content. Searching for effective strategy combinations produces an average gain of 20.9 CIDEr points over the baseline. The stated implication is that context configuration can substantially affect captioning performance, and that insights from language-only in-context learning need examination in a multimodal setting.
neurips-2023-exploring-diverse-in-contex.tldr: Systematically configuring example images and captions improves in-context image captioning, with a reported average gain of 20.9 CIDEr points over the baseline.

paragraphs: The maximum independent set problem asks for the largest collection of graph vertices with no edges connecting any pair in the collection. This paper develops a graph neural network framework inspired by dynamic programming. It turns solving the original graph into a sequence of decisions about smaller graphs, with learned comparisons guiding the recursive process.

At each step, the algorithm constructs two smaller subgraphs and predicts which has the larger maximum independent set. It then continues recursively using the selected subgraph. Training this decision rule requires comparisons labeled by relative solution size. Instead of relying only on externally supplied comparisons, the method uses its own algorithm outputs to annotate them.

This creates a self-training loop: improved predictions support more accurate comparison labels, which in turn support further training. The paper supplies numerical evidence that the approach outperforms prior methods across multiple synthetic and real-world datasets. The stated result is empirical, demonstrating the usefulness of combining recursive problem reduction with self-generated supervision rather than establishing universally optimal solutions for arbitrary graphs.
neurips-2023-maximum-independent-set-sel.tldr: A graph neural network learns to solve maximum independent set problems through recursive subgraph comparisons and self-generated training labels.

paragraphs: Discovering a compact equation for a nonlinear dynamical system requires selecting which candidate terms actually drive its behavior. The paper formulates this selection through sparse ridge regression, with an emphasis on solving the regression problem to provable optimality. OKRidge is designed to make that optimization substantially faster while retaining a certificate that the solution is optimal.

Its main technical contribution is a new lower-bound calculation derived from a saddle-point formulation. The bound can be computed through either a linear-system approach or an ADMM-based approach. In the latter, the required proximal operations reduce to another linear system and an isotonic regression problem. These calculations provide the optimization machinery used by the solver.

The authors also use beam search to warm-start the algorithm, supplying an initial candidate to help the optimization proceed. In experiments, their methods reach provable optimality with runtimes orders of magnitude below existing mixed-integer formulations solved using Gurobi. This result supports faster exact sparse model selection in the tested problems, where identifying a small set of governing terms is the scientific objective.
neurips-2023-okridge-scalable-optimal-k-.tldr: OKRidge accelerates provably optimal sparse ridge regression using new lower bounds and beam-search initialization.

paragraphs: Adapting a large vision-language model can involve training only a small number of parameters while still leaving inference expensive. This paper targets both costs together. Its objective is transfer learning that limits trainable parameters and also removes computation that is redundant for a downstream task, so adaptation efficiency carries through to using the resulting model.

The proposed dynamic architecture skipping method first uses reinforcement learning to assess how important different model modules are for the target task. It then uses the resulting rewards to skip redundant modules with lightweight adapter networks. This connects decisions about which computation to retain with the task being learned, while keeping the trainable parameter scale controlled.

The authors apply the method to ViLT and METER and evaluate it on several vision-language tasks. They report competitive performance and parameter counts relative to existing parameter-efficient methods, alongside reduced computational complexity. One stated result is an 11.97% reduction in METER's FLOPs on VQA2.0. The evidence supports treating inference computation as a separate adaptation objective alongside the number of parameters updated.
neurips-2023-parameter-and-computation-e.tldr: Dynamic architecture skipping adapts vision-language models with few trainable parameters while reducing task-specific inference computation.

paragraphs: Robots often have to act without knowing the full state of their environment, while their actions can have uncertain outcomes. Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes provide a framework for these decisions. However, long planning horizons and evolving environments remain difficult for approximate solvers. This paper modifies the planning objective to make use of a supplied reference policy.

A Reference-Based POMDP balances expected total reward against closeness to that stochastic reference policy. Its optimal policy can be computed through iterative expectations using the reference. This avoids exhaustive action enumeration at every belief node in the search tree, where a belief represents uncertainty about the current state. The reference therefore participates directly in the computational formulation.

The authors establish a theoretical relationship between standard POMDPs under stochastic policies and their reference-based formulation. They also introduce RefSolver as a basic demonstration of how to exploit it. On tested long-horizon navigation problems, RefSolver substantially outperforms POMCP. The result supports the feasibility of the modified objective and its associated computation for those planning settings.
neurips-2023-reference-based-pomdps-7e12.tldr: Reference-Based POMDPs balance reward with closeness to a reference policy, enabling an alternative computation for planning under partial observability.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning trains from a fixed dataset, but the learned policy may choose actions unlike those represented in that data. Excessive generalization can then produce incorrect value estimates. This paper examines the problem through learned representations, motivated by the observation that much of the benefit of existing conservative penalties comes from how they change those representations.

The authors study learning dynamics and formalize generalization before proposing Representation Distinction, a plug-in method. RD explicitly separates representations of dataset state-action pairs from out-of-distribution pairs produced by the learning policy. The aim is to control how broadly information transfers in the representation, addressing the source of erroneous value estimates.

The method also includes dynamic adjustment using an out-of-distribution data generator. This addresses cases where the learned policy resembles the behavior policy, making rigid separation liable to distinguish similar samples incorrectly. The authors report that RD improves specially designed and widely used offline learning algorithms on D4RL continuous control tasks, surpassing several state-of-the-art approaches in those evaluations.
neurips-2023-reining-generalization-in-o.tldr: Representation Distinction improves offline reinforcement learning by adaptively separating representations of dataset examples and out-of-distribution policy choices.

paragraphs: Audio-visual video parsing identifies events and locates where they occur in sound and images. With weak supervision, labels describe an entire video even though adjacent one-second segments can contain different events. This paper focuses on the resulting segment-level label noise, which approaches centered on cleaning overall video labels can leave unresolved.

The authors use language to describe possible combinations of events within a segment. For each video, they construct prompts covering the different cases of event appearance and compare these prompts with individual segments. The events associated with the most similar prompt become the segment's provisional label. Language provides a flexible way to express combinations beyond a single fixed event label.

Because this matching can still mislabel segments, the method dynamically reweights unreliable ones to adjust their labels. The reported experiments show a large improvement over state-of-the-art methods. The result supports addressing weak supervision at the temporal scale where events actually change, with language-based matching and subsequent correction working together to produce more useful segment-level supervision.
neurips-2023-revisit-weakly-supervised-a.tldr: Language prompts and dynamic reweighting improve weakly supervised video parsing by assigning and correcting event labels for individual segments.

paragraphs: Score-based generative models commonly use Gaussian noise associated with Brownian motion. This paper investigates a different stochastic process, motivated by sampling speed and diversity problems, including mode collapse on imbalanced data. Its Lévy-Itō Model uses isotropic alpha-stable Lévy processes, whose heavy-tailed behavior provides a different foundation for injecting and reversing noise.

The authors derive an exact reverse-time stochastic differential equation driven by the Lévy process and develop a corresponding fractional denoising score-matching method. These two pieces connect the chosen forward noise process to a trainable reverse generation procedure. The contribution therefore includes both the mathematical formulation and an experimental generative model using it.

Across CIFAR10, CelebA, and imbalanced CIFAR10LT, the experiments report faster, more diverse sampling while retaining high fidelity. On CelebA with the same architecture, LIM achieves FID 1.58 and recall 0.7006, compared with DDPM's 3.21 and 0.6437. The authors report best performance at 500 function evaluations and twice the baseline's wall-clock speed. These findings support the tested heavy-tailed alternative without resolving which stochastic process is universally optimal.
neurips-2023-score-based-generative-mode.tldr: The Lévy-Itō Model replaces Brownian noise with heavy-tailed Lévy processes and reports faster, more diverse high-fidelity image generation.

paragraphs: Observational data can leave causal effects uncertain when unmeasured factors influence both treatment and outcome. Sensitivity analysis asks how conclusions change when the assumption of no unobserved confounding is relaxed. This paper develops a unified framework for calculating sharp bounds: ranges that tightly describe the causal effects compatible with the chosen sensitivity model.

The authors generalize the marginal sensitivity model to cover a broad set of effects and treatments. The framework includes average and conditional average treatment effects, mediation and path effects, and distributional effects. It also handles discrete, continuous, and time-varying treatments. This expands sharp-bound analysis beyond simpler settings such as a single binary treatment.

The key interpretation treats uncertainty from hidden confounding as a distribution shift in latent confounders when evaluating a causal effect. For a single binary treatment, the resulting average-effect bounds agree with recent optimality results. A scalable estimation algorithm brings the framework to observational data. The bounds quantify what remains identifiable under the specified sensitivity model rather than assuming hidden confounding has disappeared.
neurips-2023-sharp-bounds-for-generalize.tldr: A generalized sensitivity framework derives sharp causal-effect bounds under unobserved confounding across varied treatments and causal questions.

paragraphs: Visual correspondence means finding how objects or parts in one image relate to those in another. Motion, occlusion, changing viewpoints, and appearance changes make this difficult. Siamese Masked Autoencoders learn correspondence from video by asking a model to reconstruct missing content in a later frame while providing an earlier frame as context.

SiamMAE samples pairs of video frames and treats them asymmetrically: the earlier frame remains intact, while 95% of patches in the later frame are masked. An encoder processes the frames independently, and a decoder uses cross-attention to predict the missing later-frame patches. This setup encourages attention to object motion and the learning of object-centered representations.

The learned features outperform state-of-the-art self-supervised methods on video object segmentation, pose keypoint propagation, and semantic part propagation. These tasks test whether information about objects and their parts can transfer across frames. The authors achieve competitive results without data augmentation, handcrafted tracking pretext tasks, or additional techniques for preventing representation collapse, supporting the usefulness of the asymmetric reconstruction objective itself.
neurips-2023-siamese-masked-autoencoders.tldr: SiamMAE learns visual correspondence by reconstructing a heavily masked future frame using an intact past frame.

paragraphs: Learning a directed acyclic graph from observational data involves uncertainty about which relationships between variables are supported. PARNI-DAG takes a fully Bayesian approach by approximately sampling graphs from their posterior distribution. Its stated setup assumes causal sufficiency, so the treatment of graph structure rests on the assumption that relevant shared causes are accounted for.

The sampler uses proposals built from adaptive random neighborhoods and local information. These proposals aim to improve mixing, meaning the sampler's ability to move through plausible graph structures. To scale with the number of variables, a preliminary tuning procedure uses a skeleton graph obtained from an existing constraint-based or score-based algorithm.

Together, these mechanisms help the sampler reach high-probability regions quickly and reduce its tendency to become trapped in local modes, including high-dimensional settings with strongly correlated variables. Experiments demonstrate mixing efficiency and accuracy in learning graph structures. The contribution is an improved procedure for exploring posterior uncertainty over graphs, with approximate sampling and causal sufficiency remaining explicit parts of its scope.
neurips-2023-structure-learning-with-ada.tldr: PARNI-DAG improves Bayesian graph-structure sampling through adaptive local proposals and skeleton-based tuning under causal sufficiency.

paragraphs: Offline reinforcement learning can overestimate the value of actions poorly represented in its fixed dataset. Value penalties aim to control this problem, but they can also affect actions that the data support. Supported Value Regularization separates these effects: it penalizes out-of-distribution action values while preserving standard Bellman updates for in-distribution actions.

The method uses the bias of importance sampling to compute a sum of Q-values across the out-of-distribution region. That sum supplies the policy-evaluation penalty and automatically creates the desired separation. In tabular Markov decision processes, the authors prove that the evaluation operator is a contraction, with a fixed point giving unbiased supported-action values and underestimated unsupported-action values.

Also in the tabular setting, policy iteration strictly improves the policy until it reaches the optimal policy constrained to the dataset's support. This is a support-constrained guarantee, so its target depends on which actions the dataset supports. Experiments validate the theoretical properties in a tabular maze and report state-of-the-art performance on a range of D4RL continuous control tasks.
neurips-2023-supported-value-regularizat.tldr: Supported Value Regularization penalizes unsupported actions while preserving supported-action updates, with tabular guarantees of convergence to the optimal support-constrained policy.

paragraphs: ToMCAT collects observations of forty three-person teams carrying out simulated urban search-and-rescue missions in a Minecraft-based environment. The dataset is intended to support studying how people coordinate, communicate, and work together. Its central feature is time synchronization across many kinds of measurements, allowing different aspects of team activity to be examined together.

Recorded modalities include fNIRS and EEG brain measurements, skin conductance, heart rate, eye tracking, face images, and spoken dialogue with automatic transcriptions. The collection also includes screenshots, gameplay and performance records, demographics, and questionnaires. Each team participates in up to six consecutive phases: three behavioral tasks, a mission training session, and two collaborative rescue missions.

This combination offers data for questions about teamwork, plan recognition, emotion, physiological linkage, entrainment, and dialogue understanding. The authors provide an initial public release of de-identified data and analyses illustrating its utility for computer science and social science. The contribution is a coordinated observational resource across tasks and modalities, with the teamwork taking place in the stated simulated setting.
neurips-2023-the-tomcat-dataset-c3884114.tldr: ToMCAT provides synchronized behavioral, conversational, and physiological data from forty teams performing simulated search-and-rescue missions.

paragraphs: A neural network's architecture determines which relationships in data it can readily capture. This paper asks what makes a data distribution suitable for locally connected networks, a family including convolutional networks, recurrent networks, and local self-attention models. It brings tools from quantum physics to a question about the match between data structure and predictive architecture.

The central theorem concerns a particular locally connected neural network. It states that accurate prediction is possible if and only if the data distribution has low quantum entanglement under specified canonical partitions of its features. Entanglement serves here as a theoretical property of the distribution across those partitions. Both the particular network and the specified partitions are part of the result's scope.

The authors turn this characterization into a preprocessing method intended to make data more suitable for locally connected networks. Experiments with widely used models on several datasets support their findings. The work therefore connects a formal necessary-and-sufficient condition to a practical intervention, while illustrating how concepts from physics can help explain relationships between learning architectures and data.
neurips-2023-what-makes-data-suitable-fo.tldr: The paper characterizes accurate prediction by a particular locally connected network through low quantum entanglement and derives a data-preprocessing method.

paragraphs: An anomaly detector must distinguish unusual examples from whatever currently counts as normal. When the normal distribution changes, training examples for that new setting may be unavailable. Adaptive Centered Representations addresses this situation through zero-shot batch-level anomaly detection, aiming to transfer learned detection behavior to previously unseen tasks without task-specific training data.

The approach combines batch normalization with meta-training over a set of related data distributions. It trains existing deep anomaly detectors, including deep SVDD, to adapt across those distributions. Exposure to related tasks and the use of batch normalization together form the proposed recipe for automatic generalization when the detector encounters a new anomaly-detection setting.

The authors report the first zero-shot anomaly-detection results for tabular data and improvements over existing methods for image anomaly detection and segmentation in specialized domains. These findings support the versatility of a relatively simple modification to established detectors. The stated setting is batch-level detection after training on interrelated distributions, which defines the context for the reported zero-shot transfer.
neurips-2023-zero-shot-anomaly-detection.tldr: Adaptive Centered Representations combines batch normalization and meta-training to transfer anomaly detectors to unseen batch-level tasks without new-task training data.
